subjects.description: small red rectangular block hanging from the spring

observation.what_happens: A small red block suspended from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the centre of the frame. The oscillation starts with the spring extended and continues uninterrupted through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is a straight vertical line with ~0.55-0.6 s period and slow amplitude decay from ~200 px span, classic mass-spring in air on Earth. Candidates go from textbook undamped SHM to viscous damped, then add quadratic air drag and cubic spring nonlinearity to explain amplitude-dependent decay and frequency.

critique.finding: The block hangs on a spring swinging with rhythm {omega} around rest spot {s_eq} while drag {gamma} drains energy. It only partly captures the motion, leaving large regular misses.
critique.headline: Spring block keeps bouncing but theory misses pattern
critique.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction alongside viscous drag to allow a straighter amplitude decay. The misses alternate sign with a widening envelope, pointing to the wrong envelope shape rather than random noise.
critique.why_it_won: It keeps gentle drag that the ideal spring lacks, without extra bends and drags that add nothing to the fit.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, sealed before the run: a linear spring with dry friction and a drive. Missed: no model proposed the drive; the miss is published.
finding: The block hangs on a spring swinging with rhythm about 12 1/s around rest spot about 78 px while drag about 0.5 1/s drains energy. It only partly captures the motion, leaving large regular misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - estimated from visual oscillation period and decay envelope over ~7 s (300 frames at 42.9 fps) without calibrated pixel scale
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical damped harmonic oscillator about static gravity-sagged equilibrium: acceleration equals -omega squared times displacement from s_eq minus gamma times velocity, with omega = sqrt(k/m) and gamma = c/m, giving underdamped sinusoid with exponential decay

turns.reasoning:
Analyzing spring oscillation data and proposing Coulomb friction to fix linear amplitude decay vs exponential model.
Extending the damping model to include Coulomb friction and estimating its deceleration parameter.
Deriving the per-cycle amplitude drop and choosing a smoothed sign function for Coulomb friction.
turns.law: Damped spring with viscous plus dry Coulomb friction

turns.reasoning:
Analyzing binned residuals showing reduced magnitude but persistent alternating oscillation despite similar overall RMS.
Attributing residual oscillation to integrator chatter at the Coulomb sign discontinuity and phase mismatch.
Testing a tanh-smoothed Coulomb term to remove the discontinuity while keeping viscous damping.
turns.law: Damped spring with viscous plus smoothed dry Coulomb friction

turns.reasoning: Choosing the original sign-based Coulomb friction model over the smoothed version due to better generalization and fewer parameters despite similar RMS.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6604980) and sealed before the run: its SHA-256 was committed and pushed in 4b94c8b, the law revealed in 9997e76. Missed. The drawn law was a linear spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive; Ansatz's winner was Muse Spark's viscously damped spring. Muse Wonder, asked by the referee, added dry friction (the right damping) but its law did worse on the unseen frames and lost; no model proposed the drive. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 15.86); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.349)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.402)
